import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1003

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1003](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1003)
-/

namespace Erdos1003

open scoped Nat
open Filter

/--
Are there infinitely many solutions to $\phi(n) = \phi(n+1)$, where $\phi$ is the Euler totient
function?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1003 : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Infinite {n | φ n = φ (n + 1)} := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős [Er85e] says that, presumably, for every $k \geq 1$ the equation
$$\phi(n) = \phi(n+1) = \cdots = \phi (n+k)$$ has infinitely many solutions.

[Er85e] Erdős, P., _Some problems and results in number theory_. Number theory and combinatorics. Japan 1984 (Tokyo, Okayama and Kyoto, 1984) (1985), 65-87.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1003.variants.Icc :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, {n | ∀ i ∈ Set.Icc 1 k, φ n = φ (n + i)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős, Pomerance, and Sárközy [EPS87] proved that for all large $x$, the number
of $n \leq x$ with $\phi(n) = \phi(n+1)$ is at most $$\frac{x}{\exp((\log x)^{1/3})}$$.

[EPS87] Erd\H os, Paul and Pomerance, Carl and S\'ark\"ozy, Andr\'as, _On locally repeated values of certain arithmetic functions_. {II}. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1987), 1--7.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1003.variants.eps87 :  ∀ᶠ x in atTop,
    {(n : ℕ) | (n ≤ x) ∧ φ n = φ (n + 1)}.ncard ≤
      x / Real.exp ((x.log) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1003

findings.description: The [EPS87] bibliography entry combines the title of Part II with the journal and page range of Part III. Part II appeared in Acta Math. Hungar. 49 (1987), 251–259; Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 101 (1987), 1–7 is Part III. The mathematical upper bound is correctly stated.
findings.source_evidence: The bibliography at https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/1003 identifies [EPS87] as Part III. Pomerance’s publication list, https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/, distinguishes the two papers and their venues. The original upper bound is Theorem 2, p. 253, of Part II (https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-14.pdf), and is recalled in the introduction to Part III.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `{II}` to `{III}` to match the cited journal/pages and the website bibliography. Alternatively, cite the original proof in Part II with the correct publication data: Acta Math. Hungar. 49 (1987), 251–259, Theorem 2.

reformulations.difference: The chain φ(n)=φ(n+1)=⋯=φ(n+k) is encoded by comparing φ(n) with each shifted value indexed by Set.Icc 1 k, rather than explicitly asserting constancy on the entire interval [n,n+k].
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The omitted offset 0 would assert only φ(n)=φ(n). Every integer in [n,n+k] has the form n+i with 0≤i≤k, and equality with the common value φ(n) is equivalent to pairwise equality throughout that interval. For k≥1, the offset 1 also excludes n=0 because φ(0)=0≠1=φ(1), so allowing natural rather than strictly positive starting points changes no solutions. The corresponding infinitude statements were proved equivalent in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

sources_consulted: Erdős, Some problems and results in number theory (1985), pp. 66–67: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-32.pdf (text read via r.jina.ai)
Erdős–Pomerance–Sárközy, On locally repeated values of certain arithmetic functions. II, Theorem 2 and surrounding remarks: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-14.pdf (text read via r.jina.ai)
Erdős–Pomerance–Sárközy, On locally repeated values of certain arithmetic functions. III, introduction: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-15.pdf (text read via r.jina.ai)
https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/ (publication entries for Parts II and III)
review.notes: All three mathematical statements are faithful to the sources; only the bibliography needs correction. The source still records the infinitude problem as open and the upper bound as proved. Lean experiments confirmed the inferred real arithmetic and cube-root exponent, automatic positivity of solution indices, the k=1 specialization, and finiteness of the counting set for every real cutoff (so ncard’s infinite-set default is unreachable). Independent equivalence and boundary tests compile in /workspace/review/, including small totient/count evaluations and the three-term run starting at 5186.
